The square is sleepy today. My zinnias stretch in the sun.
No news from the mill. My asters nod at every breeze.
I dusted every shelf twice. The freesias watched me closely.
The pigeons are dozing on the roof. My peonies droop a little.
Such a hushed morning. My gardenias smell extra sweet today.
Nobody stopped at my stall. The carnations keep me company.
I heard a wagon creak by. It rolled off without a word.
The teahouse is quiet as a mouse. My jasmine blooms anyway.
Not one rumor all day. The foxgloves guard their silence well.
I watered all the window boxes. The geraniums drank politely.
The path is empty and warm. My daisies lean into the light.
Even the bees are whispering. My clover likes the company.
No letters, no knocks, no fuss. My lilies just stand there.
I rearranged the front pots again. The begonias seem pleased.
The fountain gurgles to itself. My iris listens all day.
A sparrow hopped through the gate. My phlox bent to greet her.
Nothing stirs but the laundry. My snapdragons sway along too.
I counted the buds on my rose. Twelve today, up from nine.
The baker's oven smells faint. My lavender needs no help.
Such a lazy afternoon. My tulips refuse to do anything.
I have no secrets today. Only damp soil and a trowel.
The clock tower chimed once. My daisies perked at the sound.
Nobody came for flowers yet. The violets do not mind.
I swept the step three times. The wind kept undoing my work.
The clouds are thin as petals. My sunflowers chase them anyway.
No gossip worth repeating. The peonies keep their own counsel.
A cat napped in my window. She crushed one marigold, gently.
The lane smells like cut grass. My sweet peas approve deeply.
I repotted the ferns this morning. They seem happier already.
The market is half asleep. My hydrangeas fill the silence.
I hung fresh ribbon on the door. It matches my chrysanthemums.
Nothing happened before noon. My pansies are still yawning.
I gave a rose to a stranger. He smiled and kept walking.
The river is slow and low. My irises drink what they can.
No visitors since breakfast. The stock flowers keep quiet too.
I found a ladybug on a stem. She stayed for an hour.
The square is calm as milk. My camellias just sit pretty.
Nobody tells me anything today. The forget-me-nots listen.
I hummed while trimming the hedge. The petunias did not object.
The sun is warm and easy. My sunflowers cannot get enough.
Such a still afternoon. Even the clover holds its breath.
I dusted off the watering can. The zinnias watched politely.
Not one rumor, not one knock. My asters bloom regardless.
The neighbor's dog trotted by. He sniffed my rosemary and left.
The air smells like rain soon. My hydrangeas would welcome it.
I sold one bunch of tulips. A quiet lady, very kind.
No news from the harbor. My sea thrift looks toward the road.
The birds are lazy today. My feeder hangs untouched still.
I swept petals off the path. The breeze put them right back.
Nothing at all is happening. My freesias find that fine.
The well water is cool today. My daisies drank and thanked me.
A butterfly crossed the garden. She picked one blossom only.
Everyone seems so relaxed. My snapdragons stand at ease.
Not a single secret to share. My irises keep theirs well.
I rearranged the window pots. Third time this week, honestly.
The teapot is still warm. My gardenias share the table.
Nobody rang the bell today. My carnations just bloom on.
I watched a cloud drift over. My foxgloves watched it with me.
No errands, no callers, no rush. My clover is thriving.
The mill wheel turns slowly. My geraniums turn toward the sun.
